lead.t: The empty rectum with a gush of stool on withdrawal, onset from birth and distension describe Hirschsprung disease, where ganglion cells are missing from the bowel wall.
lead.s: Paediatrics end of 2nd semester exam (MBPE 4300): 5 October 2021, 50 MCQs

b: Occurs in approximately 1 in 5000 live births
More common in males ; tends to be more severe in females
Siblings of affected patients have increased risk
Presentation: neonate fails to pass meconium in immediate postnatal period → obstructive constipation
Life-threatening complications: enterocolitis, fluid and electrolyte disturbances, perforation, peritonitis

snip.t: A megacolon at this age is typical for Hirschsprung disease in which the submucosal and myenteric plexuses lack ganglion cells.
Other associations: duodenal atresia and Hirschsprung disease, hypothyroidism, leukaemia, hearing and eye problems (cataract, squint), atlantoaxial instability and recurrent chest infections.
